title: Telemetry Horizon schema v1 - personal notes
content:
Quick rough notes for a compact, client-facing telemetry schema (internal codename: Horizon).

Purpose:
- Reduce client -> backend telemetry volume by pre-aggregating and compact-encoding critical signals on-device.
- Make SDK behaviour configurable via a tiny server-managed policy so we can change sampling windows without shipping a SDK release.
- Preserve enough fidelity for debugging/perf regressions but avoid PII and high-cardinality blowups.

Design constraints / non-goals:
- Must work on heavy mobile and slow-network devices (3G, high packet loss).
- Goal: <5KB/day per active user baseline for common customers, earlier will vary by workload.
- Not trying to replace full server-side traces — this is complementary.
- Avoid heavy crypto; optional signing for enterprise only.

Core idea (Horizon record):
- Small, newline-delimited records (NDJSON for JSON pathway) or small binary blobs (CBOR/FlatBuffers) for production.
- Each record represents a short aggregation window (default 15s) and contains low-cardinality buckets + histogram sketches + flags.
- Records are append-only on device; SDK flushes periodically or on lifecycle events.

Minimal record fields (v1):
- schema: "horizon.v1"  // fixed string to allow evolvability
- sdk_id: <short id>     // runtime ID for SDK binary (semver-like short)
- client_id: <short>    // pseudonymous id (hashed) or empty for anonymized mode
- ts_start: <ISO8601>    // window start
- ts_end: <ISO8601>      // window end
- counters: [["gen_ok", 42], ["latency_gt_500ms", 3]]  // small list of {k,v} pairs, keys from a server-provided whitelist
- histograms: [["resp_ms", "p0:10,p50:120,p90:300,p99:1200"]]  // compact string histogram buckets or quantile summary
- tags: ["region:us-east", "model:gptx-4q"]  // only low-cardinality, filtered by policy
- sample_seed: 12345     // deterministic seed for fraction sampling debugging
- signature: <optional base64>  // enterprise opt-in

Notes on field choices:
- counters as short arrays to minimize JSON overhead. If binary, use varint-coded tuples.
- histograms are *not* dense buckets by default; use quantile summaries (t-digest style) encoded as a short string. Exact algorithm TBD.
- tags only allowed from a server-provided allowlist to avoid card integrity issues.

On-device aggregation windows and memory model:
- Default windows: 15s micro-window aggregated into 5m rollups on-device.
- Keep two rings: current-window partial aggregator and a short LRU of recent rollups (max 10 rollups) so we can retransmit if network is flaky.
- If app goes to background, force a flush of the current window and persist to local storage.

Sampling and server config (SDK API surface):
- ServerConfig payload (small JSON, 2–5 kB max):
  - version: "v1"
  - counters_allowlist: ["gen_ok","gen_err","latency_gt_500ms"]
  - tags_allowlist: ["region","model"]
  - window_ms: 15000
  - rollup_minutes: 5
  - send_policy: {"min_interval_ms": 60000, "max_batch_kb": 8, "transport": ["https","quic"]}
  - sampling: {"fraction": 0.02, "sticky_ttl_hours": 24}  // fraction sampling with sticky user selection
  - privacy: {"anonymize_client_id": true, "hash_salt_id": "cfg-2025-11"}

- SDK functions (pseudocode):
  Telemetry.configure(serverConfig)  // apply allowlists, window, sampling
  Telemetry.recordCounter(key, delta=1)  // respects allowlist and sampling seed
  Telemetry.recordLatency(name, ms)
  Telemetry.flush(immediate=false)  // attempts best-effort upload, respects send_policy
  Telemetry.forceRollup()  // internal use for background/exit handling

Transport and retry semantics:
- Use exponential backoff with jitter for uploads. Max retries per-record: 3.
- Prefer small bursts over many tiny requests. Bundle up to max_batch_kb.
- Support HEADLESS mode where device stores encrypted blobs and uploads when on Wi-Fi/charging (enterprise opt-in).

Privacy & security:
- By default client_id is omitted (anonymized). If included it's a short hash (HMAC-SHA256 with server-supplied rotateable salt).
- Tags and counters must be allowlisted by serverConfig to prevent accidental PII capture. SDK should drop any non-allowlisted keys and emit a local debug counter for dropped-keys.
- Signature optional: enterprise customers can enable a lightweight JWT signature per-batch. Signature metadata included in separate header, not inside payload (keeps payload compact).

Encoding choices:
- Development: NDJSON human-friendly text for easier debugging.
- Production: CBOR with a minimal field table (schema id -> small int mapping) then LZ4 compress batches. Provide small serializer in SDKs.
- Consider also a base64-encoded CBOR newline-delimited fallback for systems that only accept text uploads.

Acceptance criteria / metrics:
- Per-active-user bytes/day: baseline target <5KB, stretch <2KB for low-verbosity mode.
- Server-side: 99.9th percentile ingest processing latency for Horizon records < 50ms (small little payloads).
- Signal quality: can detect a 10% regression in median generation latency at 95% confidence for customers with >1k daily requests.

Experiment ideas:
- A/B enable quantile histograms vs fixed buckets to see which gives better regression sensitivity per-byte.
- Field pruning experiment: start with 8 counter keys, see which 3 are highest value, prune others.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Consensus on histogram encoding (t-digest vs HDR vs compressed quantile sketch). Priya to run a small sim.
- How to version rolling schema transitions with old devices online for months? Need graceful fallback parsing.
- Decide encryption-at-rest for local persisted rollups (enterprise vs default).
- Server-side mapping of schema keys to human-friendly strings for debugging UIs.

Immediate next steps (for me):
- mock serverConfig and add a small serializer in the JS SDK prototype (Riley to review).
- create a quick sancheck script that synthesizes records from production latency distributions and measures bytes/day.
- PR to add allowlist enforcement + dropped-key counter metric to mobile SDKs.

Notes to self: keep the initial surface minimal. Prioritize predictable bucketing, small memory footprint, and explicit allowlists. Avoid adding free-form string fields until we have a clear use case.

End of scratch notes.
summary: Notes for a compact client telemetry format (Horizon) focusing on on-device aggregation, allowlists, sampling, and compact encoding.
